1) How are you born ?
The first step in creating a character is a big one.  Ready ?  Were you created in a cloning vat? Or .. did you get into this world naturally by hatching, parturition, mitosis, etc. ?
2) Pick a Race
3) Choose a Background that is available to your race.
4) Choose a Occupation.

5) Apply the changes from your race, background and occupation to your character on the character sheet. You can use the manual override section to apply your modifiers if needed. (Opened via the checkbox on the CS-Main Sheet.)
6) Distribute 50 XP in your skills, attributes and defenses. (You can use the XP-Tool opened via the checkbox on the CS-Main sheet for help and see the character advancement section for more info.)
7) Choose contacts, spend (or not) starting credits.
EXPERIENCE COST
Your character's skill level is equivalent to the number of XP spent in that skill.
To buy skills you must spend experience points. At character creation you can just spend this experience as you wish. New characters cannot buy skills levels over 5

Skills cost 1XP per skill level (This is cumulative, so for exemple :  buying a level 1 skill would  cost 1XP , upgrading that same skill to level 2 would be 2 XP,  so the total cost for a level 2 skill is 3XP if you would start from 0)
Experience cost for SKILLS is 1 up per skill level. You must buy every level of the skill
Attributes cost 5XP times the level of the attribute. This is also cummulative. Since primary attributes can be at 0 or in the negative the minimum cost for 1 point is always 5XP.
SKILL TRAINING

Existing characters that wish to increase their skills must seek training, this can be done by either purchasing a training course, having another character with a higher level skill teach you or with game master approval, you can increase it instantly if he thinks that you spent enough time using this skill to justify the higher level. Regardless of method, you still need to spend the experience points.
Training skills cost 10 000cr per level and take a full day per level for training. Every skill level must be purchased separately.
If you do not have the free time required to train, you can still purchase the training and progress but your progress will be three times as long.
Skill chips (EVO Cybernetics) cost 50 000cr per skill level but do not require you purchase lower level of the skills. Availability is equal to the skill level.
Example: Increasing a skill from 3 to 6 would cost a total of 15 XP and 150 000 credits. It would also take 15 days of training (or 45 if you do not take time off).
TALENTS  (See the Talent tab for more information)
Every experience point invested in a category (PHYSICAL, MENTAL, SOCIAL, ACUITY) grants the character 1 TALENT point to buy talents in that category.
Every time a Talent is purchased, the number of points available in that category will drop by the talent's cost. The total cannot go below 0.
Exemple :  If you have 4 skills at 5 in your PHYSICIAL category , you have a total of 20 points available for TALENTS in the PHYSICIAL category.
EVOLUTION ( See Evolution tab for more information)

Evolution is an optional system. No character is forced to spend resources in this system. This system serves as a way to guide players wishing to modify their body, add cybernetics components or dabble in magic.
Evolution allow characters to progress their characters by investing resources in the following areas. GENETICS, CYBERNETICS or MAGIC
Every character has 10 evolution points. Each tiers cost their rank in number EVO of points. Those points serve to limit how a character evolves.

Evolution has 3 tiers per category, before you can purchase a higher tier of EVO you must first buy the previous tier in that category. (Exemple : To get Alpha Specimen TIER II, you also need Alpha Specimen TIER I and the total EVO cost would be 3 EVO (1+2) points out of your maximum of 10 EVO points.)
Tier 1 evolutions grant some benefits but usually have a pretty small impact on actual gameplay.
Tier 2 evolutions are substantial enough that while they grant significant changes to a character they also have some minor drawbacks
Tier 3 evolutions require total dedication to a specific evolution category. They provide major benefits to a character but come with significant drawbacks.
Evolution traits cost 1 point per tier so if a player wishes to acquire a tier 3 trait, as the tier 3 requires both tier 1 and 2, the toal cost will be 6 points.
BENEFITS AND DRAWBACKS OF EVOLUTION
GENETICS

Tier 1  - Your new genetic code has had some cosmetic changes on your appearance; pick one or more feature from your appearance (color, shape, feature like hair, or horns and mutate them in some way).
Tier 2 - Lifebane critical effect will disable one of your GENETIC EVO's (Player's choice but all 3 tiers) until a recovery roll is made

Tier 3 - Extensive genetic modifications can have a severe impact on drugs and medical treatment. Any drug or medical item used on you has a 50% chance of having no TOXICITY or double TOXICITY. You can order custom drugs to avoid this effect.
CYBERNETICS

Tier 1 - Replacing body parts with machinery does leave some traces. You now have some visible implants on your body. Pick one or more feature from your appearance that represents your Cybernetic EVO (you can customize it to some extent).
Tier 2 - EMP critical effect will disable one of your CYBERNETIC EVO's (Player's choice all 3 tiers) until a recovery roll is made.

Tier 3 - You now count as a MACHINE and no longer COUNT as a LIVING BEING. When you suffer a SEVERE TRAUMA you have a 50% chance that it will instead strike one of your cybernetic EVO's : Negate the TRAUMA and one of your Cybernetic EVO (Player's choice, all 3 tiers) is disabled until repaired.
Passive: Effects that are always on, generates no CYBER SHOCK

Active: Free action to gain the benefits of an active effect, player must roll for CYBER SHOCK: When activating a Cybernetics augment you risk CYBER SHOCK. To avoid this you must roll a TECHNOLOGY skill Vs your curent MORALE value to see if the augment performs normally. Should you fail, the augment works and you lose 1 morale per TIER of this augment. If your morale drops to 0 you lose control of your character.
MAGIC
Tier 1 - EVO magic is done via spirit fusion as tattoos or grafting relics into your flesh. Pick the design and modify one or more of your character's features to reflect this new appearance.
Tier 2 - Spiritbane critical effect will disable one of your MAGIC EVO's (Player's choice all 3 tiers) until a recovery roll is made.

Tier 3 - You no longer count as a LIVING being  while your SPIRIT is active, you instead count as a SPIRIT. Because of your supernatural composure you leak CHI in your environment: Every SCENE you start in has at least 1 RAW CHI in the area.
CHALLENGE / TURN ORDER
At the start of a challenge determine if either side is surprised, if no side has surprise challenge order normally (players first).
In the case of surprise, turn order is inverted, enemies will go first for the entire scene.
When surprised, during the first round, the defending party is limited to a STANDARD or MOVE action only.
Initiative is only rolled when an action would opposed another action. See INTERRUPT and REACTION
1 - MAINTENANCE PHASE Perform RECOVER against all AILMENTS affecting you and maintain/sustain or end any effects requiring you to do so.
2 - QUICK ACTIONS *Can be performed at any point in the round but always after maintenance phase.
3 - MOVEMENT ACTIONS Can be delayed; when delayed you move in Phase 8 at the end of the round.
4 - STANDARD ACTIONS
5 - ENEMY TURN (or players' turn if turn order is reversed due to surprise)
6 - COMPLEX ACTIONS players are first unless turn order is reversed due to surprise.
7 - BONUS ACTIONS (if applicable). I.e.: SURGES or powers granting additional actions
8 - ADDITIONAL MOVEMENT If you have not yet used your MOVE or if your are RUNNING you can now use it.
DICE SUCCESS
Unless specified, a success on a D10 dice, is always on a 5+  (failures are on 1,2,3,4)

All weapons have a DMG and POWER value.
Damage determines the amount of damage a weapon does once a hit has passed defenses.
Power determines the relative strength of the weapon and is a direct counter to DEFENSE. Every point of power above DEFENSE will deny SOAK and under will reduce damage by the same amount.
All armors have a SOAK and DEFLECT value.
SOAK is the ability of a forcefield or Armor to reduce the damage of an attack. If the damage is reduced to 0 the attack is considered fully absorbed and no other effects are checked.

Deflect gets added to your DEFENSE (along cover and other modifiers) to counter POWER and determine how much damage penetrates or is negated by the armor. A higher value will reduce damage while a lower value will hinder your ability to SOAK damage properly.
Roll DAMAGE

Does the enemy have a forcefield active ? If yes, is your DAMAGE above the Forcefield's SOAK value ?   No : the forcefield prevents your attack and has it's soak value reduced by your damage.   Yes :  The forcefield breaks and prevents your attack.
There is no forcefield active ?
Compare the POWER value against the DEFLECT value.  If POWER is above DEFLECT, the difference is automatic damage dealt. If DEFLECT is above POWER, the difference is automatic damage reduction.
Roll SOAK + Endurance
Compare the remaining damage to the soak+endurance value and the unmitigated damage is removed from HEALTH.
Any damage exceeding a target's Endurance (after mitigation) will trigger Critical Ailments and apply TRAUMA.
DEVIATION

SURGE
At the start of every game you have 1 surge point.
Additionnal Surges are gained when players accept a bad consequence or can be given up to cancel that consequence.
The maximum amount of surges you can hold at once is equal to the highest between ENDURANCE or WILLPOWER. Additional surges gained over that value are lost.
Players cannot spend more than their (pick either SPEED or WITS) surges per SCENE.

Time and dates around the Galaxy
In 56 due to Galactic time differences, planet sizes etc. a standard measuring system was adopted
a day is 10 hours
a week is 10 days
a month is 10 weeks or 100 days
a year is 10 months or 100 weeks or 1000 days
Days and months have no official names, most call them by their numbers i.e.: day 8 month 8 year 5734 (08-08-5734)
Full time employment is 10 hours of work (a day) then 10 hours off (a day) you end up working 50% of the time or 50 hours a week.
Armors provide protection against all forms of attacks. The type of armor determines a few factors.
FORCEFIELDS
Forcefields are invisible barriers designed to negate ranged attacks. They have no effect in melee range (except shields, see below).
Unlike armors forcefields only have SOAK and no Deflect but that SOAK is guaranteed (reduce damage by forcefield value before you check for armor).
When damage exceeds the value of a shield or forcefield you ignore the rest of the hit no matter how much damage is left. (ie: shield gating).
Shields :       Provide frontal protection (no effect vs flank and back hits) against various ranged attacks and also in melee range against one opponent of your choice.
Combat :       Forcefield designed for combat situations, provides some protection with a quick recharge time.
Guardian :     Very high deflection forcefields designed to negate surprise and initial attacks. They lack any staying power for long term engagements.
Generators : Stationary generators designed to protect valuable positions and everyone inside.

In the case of a negative PHYSICAL attribute value you reduce your power and damage instead of increasing it.
Two handed weapons also gain damage dices in addition to the power. (or reduces power and damage if PHYSIQUE is negative)

SPIRITS
Your SPIRIT determines your BARRIER, SPIRIT POWER and Maximum spells.
If you do not have a spirit you can't manifest spells or powers but you can use relics. Relics do not require SPIRIT
Each SPIRIT has a maximum number of SPELLS, BARRIERS and SPIRIT POWER.
Only GOD spirits can old all powers from a DOMAIN but cannot use any SPELLS, POWER or BARRIERS from a different DOMAIN.

A SPIRIT can be SUPPRESSED.

While SUPPRESSED, any actions you perform first require a Willpower check (DC = shooters accuracy). On success you can act normally. On failure lose 1 morale and you are forced to use the next action to either move out of the cover fire area or move into better cover within the area. If either option is unavailable you must go PRONE on your location and cannot move.
Manifesting or supressing your SPIRIT is a STANDARD action.
GAINING A NEW SPIRIT OR UPGRADING A SPIRIT.
In order to acquire a spirit a player must either bind another spellcaster and kill him, try to call one using raw CHI or destroy a relic to manifest its spirit.
New spirits always come with a single spell, it is up to you to acquire new ones.
Binding another spellcaster's spirit
To bind a spirit you must succeed at a BINDING DC is set by the current CHI of the opponent.

Once bound. your target's spirit will be available to you once it's owner is dead; if you already have a spirit when that happens you can chose to replace yours or change your mind and let the spirit disappear.

Gaining a spirit by binding someone else's strips the new spirit of most of its spells, the new spirit only comes with 1 spell (from it's owners repertoire) but the spirit domain, tier, barrier and spirit power remain the same.
You can spend a standard action to undo a bind, the DC is the result of the initial BIND check.
You can also bind the spirit to a relic that has been prepared in advance instead of yourself. Spirit will then power the relic on the death of its owner, rules are otherwise the same.
Calling a spirit with RAW CHI
To manifest a spirit from RAW chi and bind it to yourself, you must perform a SPIRITUAL skill check Vs DC value of the RAW CHI pool.
If you would rather bind the spirit to a RELIC replace the SPIRITUAL skill checks with BINDING ones. (Requires an appropriate relic to store the spirit).

The domain of the spirit being called is random, its tier and DC is based on the RAW chi pool (1-3 = Minor, 4-6 = Intermediate, 7-9 = Major and 10 = god), the barrier and spirit power are randomly rolled once the domain has been established.
Bringing a spirit from RAW chi always trigger a SPIRITUAL control check (or BINDING if binding it to a relic), if you succeed you gain the spirit, if you fail check the BACKLASH table
If you succeed you manifest the spirit and can take it as your own replacing any existing ones you have.
Destroying a relic

You can perform a BINDING skill check to destroy a relic and acquire the spirit inside. Spirits acquired this way have their domain, barrier and spirit power predetermined but they come with no spells
DC of the binding check is the same as the one to make that relic. Only try relics can be used, relic shards do not contain a spirit.
If you fail the Binding, the relic is destroyed but you do not acquire the spirit.
Upgrading a SPIRIT to a higher tier
A spirit you own can be upgraded to a higher tier once it knows the maximum amount of spells it can.
To upgrade you perform the same steps as when calling a spirit with RAW chi however the minimum RAW CHI of the pool must meet the tier of the new spirit rank.
For example when upgrading from a Minor spirit to and Intermediate, you would need a minimum RAW chi pool of 4 (Minimum required to summon Intermediate spirits).
If you succeed your spirit gains the new rank, you will have to max out his new spells before you can attempt another upgrade. Should you fail, your spirit loses one of its spells
Upgrading spirits can only be done with RAW CHI. Otherwise you muse acquire a new spirit via Relic or be Binding someone else's spirit.
CHI

Players by default have 5 personnal CHI unless stated otherwise or modified by RACE / Backgrounds / EVO or Talents. Maximum CHI for anyone is 10, any CHI increase past that point are lost unless specified/temporary.
Raw CHI is the accumulated CHI in your immediate environment.
Personnal CHI is restored when you take a short rest (typically 5 minutes of rest)
SPELLS cost an equivalent amount of CHI to the level they invoked (Minor = 1 , Intermediate = 2 , Major = 3)

When any spell is cast using your own personnal CHI, immediately add the personal CHI spent to the RAW CHI pool (this CHI is added even if the spells fails). This raw CHI pool persists for the duration of the scene or up to normally around 5 minutes (can be more, DM's choice).
Multiple people casting spells all add up in the same RAW CHI pool.
Spells cast using relics do not contribute CHI in the RAW pool. Critical failures using spell shards still triggers a control check.
The RAW CHI pool can never exceed 10 CHI, any CHI added past that point is lost.
Casting spells from RAW CHI lowers the value of the raw CHI pool by that same amount.
When casting with RAW CHI you automatically trigger a control check; see control check for details
SPELLS
To cast a spell you can use your personal CHI or Raw CHI. Relics do not use CHI.
To cast a SPELL, choose the level of the SPELL to be cast and then roll the associated SKILL.  Each spell has their own conditions for SUCCESS.
Casting or maintaining spells with your own CHI follows normal rules. You only trigger a control check on a critical failure.
Casting or maintaining spells with a relic's follows the same rules as above but also drains the relic rendering it inactive for a time period depending on the relic type, setting it on cooldown.

Any SPELL with a BUFF component or a SUSTAIN effect can be maintained. Every round during maintenance you announce if you SUSTAIN the effect or not. Players cannot have more than 1 SUSTAIN effect at a time. SUSTAINING an effect does not cost CHI.
SPIRIT POWERS
Spirit powers do not cost CHI, they do however require actions and are specific to your Spirit type.
BARRIERS
Barriers are always active when your SPIRIT is not SUPRESSED. NO roll is required  however Barriers minor, intermediate and major powers are a BUFF and require a SKILL check and to be SUSTAINED.
COUNTER SPELL

Counter spell: To counter a spell a player must use a QUICK action to perform an immediate interrupt and win the INITIATIVE, followed by a SPIRITUAL skill check Vs other caster's result. Should either the initiative or spiritual check fail then they were either too slow or too weak to counter the effect.

Counter spell: Players can also counter spell using the same magic type as the caster (PRIMALIST,CHRONOMANCY, SOOTHSAYER, ELEMENTALIST), this grants a SMALL bonus or the exact same spell, this grants a LARGE bonus.
LEARNING/REPLACING SPELLS
To acquire new spells you can do the following 3 things: Absorb a counter spell, create a new one from RAW CHI or consume a relic shard.
In all 3 cases you must have a spirit with a free spell slot open or a relic shard before you can try to acquire any spells.
As a complex action you can sacrifice a spell to free up a spell slot.
If you successfully counter spell you gain the exact spell you countered.
Consuming a relic shards grant the exact same spell inside the shard with a successful BINDING check

Making a spell with RAW chi requires a SPIRITUAL control check. The value of the RAW chi pool determines what type of spell you can create. On success you acquire the spell, barrier or power, on failure nothing happens.
The RAW CHI pool determines the rarity of the spells, barriers and spirit powers you can acquire.
RAW CHI pool 1-2 : Random domain, COMMON powers only

HACKING, How technology and networks work in the 56th century.

In the 56th century almost every manufactured object can communicate, and therefore be hacked. Even mundane items like clothing carry basic functions: heat regulation, moisture control, self-cleaning routines. A DATACOM helps them communicate with each other for optimal efficiency. This is what hackers exploit, and also what protects you against them.

Evolution is an optional system. No character is forced to spend resources in this system. It serves as a way to guide players wishing to modify their body, add cybernetics, or dabble in magic.

Every character can have as many EVOs as they can take. Each tier adds its rank to the total EVO points a character has. Those points dictate the severity of consequences tied to having too many EVOs.

Evolution has 3 tiers per category. Before buying a higher tier you must first buy the previous tier in that category. (e.g. To get Alpha Specimen TIER II you also need TIER I — total EVO point increase would be 3.)
Tier 1 evolutions grant some benefits but usually have a small impact on actual gameplay.
Tier 2 evolutions are substantial and grant significant changes to a character.
Tier 3 evolutions provide major benefits but come with a significant cost to credits and EVO total.
Evolution traits add 1 point per tier to your EVO score. If a player acquires a Tier 3 trait (which requires Tiers 1 and 2), the total increase will be 6 points.
Skills required to install an EVO: Medical for Genetics, Technology for Cybernetics, Binding for Magic. Install DC is 2, 4, or 6 depending on EVO tier.
There is no hard limit to the number of EVOs a character can have, but past a certain point there is a significant chance of consequences ranging from minor annoyances to full psychosis.
When installing EVOs, compare the total EVO ranks (including the new EVO) against the sum of ENDURANCE + WILLPOWER. If the result is 0 or negative, the body accepts the EVO without complications.

When Attributes Vs EVO is 1 or more, the GM secretly rolls a D10 and subtracts any additional successes the installer got over the install DC. If the GM's total is 1 or more, the recipient gains an EVO affliction.
Afflictions do not manifest right away — a player will never know how bad it is until it is too late.
Triggered when a player makes a critical failure during a SCENE from a roll that could have been influenced by their EVO.
EVO afflictions will never trigger more than once per SCENE.
EVO afflictions are cumulative. When multiple are possible the GM rolls which activates randomly.
Getting cloned resets all of a character's EVOs and any afflictions acquired. Permanent EVOs remain forever.
An EVO can never negate the drawback from one of the afflictions. If an EVO would normally render you immune, you ignore that EVO.

Gain a LARGE damage bonus Vs LIVING targets. Critical ailment with LIFEBANE apply the SICK ailment, if the ailment is already present, deal a TRAUMA instead.
Leadership can heal one point of morale. DC of the check is equal to the target's missing MORALE
Legality class determines whether it is legal or not to carry such an item under the alliance law. Outside of the alliance, laws are usually localized.
Provide basic protection and counts as a SMALL item for encumbrance. Requires 1 rounds to put on or remove.
SMALL PENALTY or LOW to MEDIUM DEFENSE | Small appliances, a trashcan, small trees, lamppost, a car door, coffee table, plaster walls etc.

A datacom, server or device which you are directly using by being physically connected to. Being physically connected automatically bypass the NETWORK and you instead deals with the local device defenses.
While under the effect of lockon a target cannot stealth and will always grant line of sight (cover still applies).
Always get maximum SOAK rolls when defending against SPIRITUAL attacks.
Critical hits have no additional effects. Masterwork has no effect if the wearer is BREACHED.

Players can carry a limited number of objects but they are also limited by WEIGHT. MAX WEIGHT is = 50 KG Modified by Physique times 5KG |  Lift = 5 time your total carry | Push or drag =  10 times your carry
Total data capacity your device can hold. Your ROUTINES, PROGRAMS and TOOLS reduce this capacity.
You get maximum SOAK when a critical faillure results in a SOAK roll. (From a DEFENSE check or other checks)
Mortal wounds cause a LARGE penalty to the following attributes: PHYSICAL, ENDURANCE, ACUITY and SPEED.

Move up to 5m in a round. You can also use a STANDARD action to move allowing for an additional movement action. If your previous action was a move you can instead RUN (see description). You can also change stance (prone, crouch) this counts as moving 1 meter.
During a round where you have moved, you gain a SMALL BONUS to your defense VS any attacks performed against you. Because you moved you also have a SMALL penalty to all skill checks.
Weapon counts as Dual Wielding (Can perform double attacks).
NANITES are a special ressources that powers nanomachines and enable and enables your DATACOM to form or interact with physical objects in the real world. NANITES recharge after a SCENE.
During maintenance phase you can spend any number of NANITES to reroll failed AILMENTS saves.
Sectors within a NEBULA experience all sorts of anomalies. Any captain should steer well away from those areas as you never know which system will stop working on your ship.
Weapon fires high velocity needles; crits automatically on a 9 or 10 and and has a SMALL bonus to damage on critical hits.

A giant nebula that spans from the ASH system all the way into Kraven space. For some reason Kravens cannot seems to traverse that area. Any exploration of the area is forbidden due to the lethal nature of the area.
Allows private sharing of anything in memory to any connected NODES within range. Any REMOTE NODE attacks against a NETWORK is done against the NETWORK CONTROLLER.

A node is a intelligentdevice that exists within a network or by itself and that has a FIREWALL and can run ROUTINES or have devices connect to it. (Datacom, intelligent devices, advanced drones, etc.)
Once per SCENE as a FREE action, when this forcefield breaks you can chose to deal 2D + 4 [HIGH] STUN PHYSICAL damage to everyone in a 2m radius. Targets hit by this attack are pushed back 2m.

A nova cruiser is a battlecruiser with enough armor to survive being hit by another battlecruiser. They are gigantic structures that resemble ships but who's main function is to provide the anchor for a fleet. Typical size is 5km length with a crew of 100+ and up to 10k passengers.
Weapon has almost no technology on board. EMP has no effect and negative or positive effect from HACKING, VIRUS and ROUTINES can not apply.
Reapply damage during maintenance phase. (No effect if damage was reduced to 0 prior to next maintenance phase)

Ordonnance weapons are ship weapons that also require ammunition. If not paired with an ammo bay the weapon has enough munitions to fire until it needs to reload.
Phase you out of reality when attacked. Gain a 1 in 10 chance of negating any attack.

BLEED : Lose 1 HEALTH per maintenance phase. (Cummulative if reapplied). Damage caused by physicaly hitting a target with another material object (bullets, melee weapons, fists). Bullets, Needles and Melee damage generally falls into this category
Power determines the relative strength of the weapon and is a direct counter to DEFENSE. Every point of power above DEFENSE will deny SOAK and under will reduce damage by the same amount.
Provide excellent protection and counts as a LARGE item for encumbrance. Requires 3 rounds to put on or remove.

You can take a SMALL penalty to a COMPLEX attack to target a specific location or object. (Can be used to hit armor weak spots, armor is treated as BREACHED for that hit but requires you to identify the armor type first via tactics)
A program is something you can use as a standard action to replace basic hacking action. Programs only cost MEMORY.
Grants GOOD COVER vs ranged attacks. Your maximum movement is 2. Your DEFENSE Vs MELEE has a LARGE penalty.
Allows the weapons to perform a SIMPLE ATTACK as a QUICK action.
Quick actions can be performed at any point during the round (including enemy turn). If you call a QUICK action during someone else's turn you must win initiative. (See INTERUPTS and REACTIONS)
Any power, weapon or item that has the QUICK keyword can be used to perform a BASIC ATTACK as a QUICK ACTION.
Datacoms have a default range of melee, 100m, 1000m (Skill penalties are  0/1/3). In Melee range you are considered connected directly.
Weapon has double base reach
Weapon incurs a cummulative penalty of +1 DC to all shots after the first. This penalty resets if you AIM or perform a STANDARD action that isin't shooting that weapon.
During maintenance you can roll 1D for every ailment you are suffering from. On a 6+ you recover, on a failure the ailment continues.

When SOAK run out a forcefield is rendered innactive. To recharge a forcefield, you must spend the time under "Regen" not being shot at. When that condition is true your forcefield returns during the next maintenance phase.
Item is a MINOR relic pick one MINOR RELIC effect on item acquisition.

Reduce damage by X of the type specified.

Resting for a period of 10 hours in a non threatening safe area will recover your ENDURANCE in HEALTH and WILLPOWER in MORALE.
Can hide up to a small object. Provides passive concealment of 5 or a LARGE bonus to an active Concealment roll.
You grant your skill roll result as a bonus to the next person's job in the job order.
You add your skill roll result as a penalty to the next person's job in the job order.
A set of instructions that can run on a datacom. ROUTINES consume CPU to stay active and provides passive benefits to anyone connected to the network.
If your last action was a move action you can replace your MOVE with a RUN action. RUN double your movement speed. If you stop at any point, you must MOVE again before running again.
When running, increase the move DEFENSE bonus to LARGE and the move SKILL check penalty to LARGE.
You gain a SMALL bonus to HIT. If you have LOCKON you this bonus is LARGE instead.
When you suffer morale damage from an attack that exceeds your willpower modifier, you gain the shaken status ailment or broken status if you were already shaken.

Gain a LARGE damage bonus Vs MAGICAL targets. Applying a critical ailment with a SPIRITBANE will reduce its MANIFESTATION level to the following depending on level :   Manifested or Awakened > Passive ,  Passive > Suppresed,  if the spirit MANIFESTATION level is already suppresed the  effect will cause a TRAUMA instead.
Scrapped indicates that an object or item stops functioning completely. Nothing works anymore, item will have to be repaired before it can be used again.
Your PHYSICAL attribute for MIGHT checks is 10. Device now counts as ELECTRONIC Vs EMP.
Shaken cause a SMALL penalty to the following attributes: MENTAL, WITS, SOCIAL and WILLPOWER.
You can use a QUICK action to move up to 1m, change your stance (crouch, stand, prone). A SHIFT does not cause opportunity attacks when used to move out of the reach of a target.
Spaceships need power for their various components, if there's a surplus it will be listed as available power. This can be used for various things like weapons, shields or various systems.
The value on your ship's cargo indicates how many units of cargo you can fit in that area. One unit of ship cargo is equal to one HUGE item.
The class of a ship determines which category it belongs to: Ship classes from smallest to largest are Drones, Fighters, Corvettes, Frigates, Cruisers, Battlecruisers, Carriers and Nova Cruisers.
The combat range is your ship's weapon range, weapons that exceed this range will have to shoot blind.
The command rating of a ship indicates how well designed it is for a leader to direct its crew. See COMMAND section under SPACE rules for details
The ship component count indicate how much space you have on a given design to add new areas and components.
The core of a ship is the most protected area of the ship and any components housed in that area will keep functioning until the ship is SCRAPPED.
Drones are short range crewless single task spaceships. They range from 510 meters and while some can handle cargo none of them can handle living things.
ECM stands for electronic counter measures and the value indicates your ship's SYSTEM damage threshold. Any system damage exceeding this value in a single hit will cause a TRAUMA.
The engineering rating of a ship indicates how much RESSOURCE UNITS it can generate and how skilled an engineer must be to operate it. See ENGINEERING section under SPACE rules for details.
Most ships operate using fusion drives which have a lifetime supply of fuel, some ships however, run on CORONTHIA a super dense fuel that produce an immense amount of power but requires refuelling.

Ships have artificial gravity as long as they have power movement inside is normal. Gravity is part of the life support component. If life support is gone then the ship is now difficult terrain (Vacuum).
The handling of a ship indicates how maneuverable it is and how difficult is it to pilot. See HANDLING section under SPACE rules for details
Hull is your ship's durability. Taking damage will lower this value. It can be repaired using resources but does not recover naturally. If your HULL reaches 0 your ship is SCRAPPED.
The instrument rating on a ship indicates how precise it can navigate its electronic warfare capabilities. See INSTRUMENTS section under SPACE rules for details
Indicates how many galactic quadrants your ship can calculate a trajectory to.
Indicates how fast you travel when at jump speed. Standard speed is a week (100 hrs) per quadrant.
This value lets you know how long your life support can handle a full load of passengers on board in optimal conditions. Having more people than life support will lead to death.

Indicates how many passengers this ship can carry. Crew and passengers count separately on a ship and will more than likely have different accommodations. Life support will also match the maximum passenger count.
The maximum crew is the amount of personal required to fully staff a ship. Anyone operating on a ship under maximum crew has a SMALL penalty to all their skill checks.
The minimum amount of personnel required on a ship to operate it. Anyone operating on a ship under minimum crew has a LARGE penalty to all their skill checks.

When repairing a ship you need to have the available resource units and perform a skill check (TECHNOLOGY for SYSTEM or JOURNEYMAN for HULL) to restore one point. Shields do not require skill checks and can instead convert X resources units to shield see SHIP SHIELD RECHARGE.
This is how far away you can detect other ships and objects. Anything beyond that range is impossible to detect.
Shields on spaceships function as damage buffer. Any damage done will impact shields first. If no shields are available then the damage goes directly into HULL or SYSTEM.
Shield recharge on a spaceship indicates how many units of power you can send to the shield to recharge an equal amount.

The speed of ships is normalized to 3 distinct values: LOW, MEDIUM and HIGH. (you can always lower your speed). Ship speed has no effect on jump range. See SHIP speed section of SPACE rules for more details.
Structure is the damage threshold that your HULL can take before you are COMPROMISED or CRIPPLED. Any hull damage exceeding this value in a single hit will cause one of those TRAUMA.

System is your ship's electronics' durability, taking system damage will lower this value. It can be repaired using resources but does not recover naturally. If your SYSTEM reaches 0 your ship is SCRAPPED.
The type of a ship determines which subclass the ship belongs to and will determine it's internal configurations, role and components.
The warfare rating on a ship indicates how advanced the weapon systems are and how difficult they are to operate. See WARFARE section under SPACE rules for details.
The sick ailment causes anyone to have a SMALL penalty to all ATTRIBUTES and DEFENSES. SICK cannot be removed through RECOVER, see the condition that applied SICK to find out how to remove it.

While STUNNED you cannot act until you RECOVER from that ailment.

An absence of air will lead to suffocation. When a character is deprived of air roll a RESILIENCE check every round at DC1, increase DC by 1 for every round thereafter until death or a source of air is found. On a failed check you lose the DC of the resilience check as health (stun dmg). DMG will not sop if you enter DYING state.

While SUPPRESSED, any actions you perform first require a Willpower check (DC = shooters accuracy). On success you can act normally. On failure lose 1 morale and you are forced to use the next action to either move out of the cover fire area or move into better cover within the area. If either option is unavailable you must go PRONE on your location and cannot move.
REMOVED : Change to consumable item (armor in a bottle)
How many HACKS it takes to render this device innactive. Any devices with no SYSTEM stat goes down in 1 HACK. Devices with 0 SYSTEM can be repaired (takes 1 scene)
Melee weapon can be thrown with a DEXTERITY skill check.
Tools and options which help can provide a small or large bonus, some actions might require tools and instead of granting a bonus, tools will negate a penalty. GM's discretion.
Total cover means that the target is fully hidden from view. You cannot try to shoot around total cover but you can still shoot through; see BAD or GOOD cover for effects.
Your ship identification and classification to other ships that can scan you. Also contains your ship name. (Registration and ship name should match... but then there's pirates).
Trauma is a keyword to indicate that the subject is suffering from an effect caused by high HEALTH or MORALE loss. LIGHT TRAUMA are GRAVE and SHAKEN. SEVERE TRAUMA is MORTAL and BROKEN

Weapons labelled as turret weapons are gimballed and can face any direction they need. Weapons that are TURRET tagged can fire even when the GUNNER is at a DISADVANTAGE. As a drawback turret weapons use up more component space and use additional power.
Device can fit any of the alliance races, in the case of ARMOR, it can be put on or removed as a COMPLEX action

How much defense against MORALE attacks your device grants.

When you suffer health damage in excess of your  endurance, you gain the grave wound status ailment; if you were already suffering from a grave wound you replace it to a mortal wound status. If you were already suffering from a mortal wound you go strait to the DYING status.
Armor defense against this weapon cannot be better than MEDIUM.
Forcefield defense against this weapon cannot be better than MEDIUM.
Ship combat follows a fixed job order, regardless of character initiative:
MAINTENANCE → COMMANDER → ENGINEER → NAVIGATOR → PILOT → GUNNER
Characters not assigned to a ship role act after ENGINEER and before NAVIGATOR using normal initiative.
Roles add +1 to +10 to all ship ratings they use. Do not assign natural 10s to ship ratings, 10 is only reachable through talents, manufacturer bonuses, and optional upgrades.

Uses LEADERSHIP vs the ship's Command rating. Success: Add the ship's Command rating as a bonus to any one job this round. Failure: That job suffers Disadvantage. Critical Failure: All jobs suffer Disadvantage this round.

Uses ENGINEERING vs the ship's Engineering rating. Success: Generate Resource Units (RU) equal to the ship's Engineering rating. Failure: Generate 0 RU. Critical Failure: Also sets Available Power = 0 for the round. Critical Success: Generate maximum skill result in RU. Engineers spend RU using TECHNOLOGY (system repairs) or CRAFT (hull repairs).

Uses NAVIGATION vs the ship's Instruments rating. On success, add the ship's Instruments rating and compare to the enemy ship. Below enemy base rating: give Disadvantage to HACKING, CYBERINTEL, OPERATOR, and PILOT. Between enemy base and total: no effect. Above enemy total: grant Advantage to those roles.

Uses PILOTING vs the ship's Handling rating. On success, add the ship's Handling rating and compare to the enemy ship. Below enemy base rating: Gunners suffer Disadvantage. Between enemy base and total: no effect. Above enemy total: Gunners gain Advantage.

Uses HEAVY WEAPONS vs the ship's Warfare rating. On success, add the ship's Warfare rating and compare to the enemy ship.

Below enemy base rating: all shots miss. Between enemy base and total: normal attack. Above enemy total: Critical Hit possible.

With Disadvantage, Fixed Weapons cannot fire. Turret Weapons can still fire but apply the penalty. Gunners act last and do not pass advantage/disadvantage to anyone.
